0.headline: SLMG Beverages, Coca Cola's largest bottler in India, eyes Rs 20,000 crore turnover in 5 yrs, IPO in 3-4 years
0.heading: SLMG Beverages, Coca Cola's largest bottler in India, eyes Rs 20,000 crore turnover in 5 yrs, IPO in 3-4 years
0.intro: The company, which holds Coca-Cola's bottling rights for high-density markets in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, looks to capitalise on India's consumption growth and also explore opportunities in overseas markets.
0.body:
SLMG Beverages, Coca-Cola's largest bottler in India, is targeting a turnover of Rs 20,000 crore within five years and plans to list on the stock exchanges before that timeline, according to its Joint Managing Director Paritosh Ladhani.

The company, which holds Coca-Cola's bottling rights for high-density markets in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, looks to capitalise on India's consumption growth and also explore opportunities in overseas markets.

"We should at least go for Rs 20,000 crore in the next five years. We will definitely be listed by then," Ladhani told PTI in an interview.

Besides, the Lucknow-based company, which currently ranks among the world's top 15 Coca-Cola bottlers, aims to break into the top 10 firms globally within five years and become one of the world's top five bottlers over the next decade.

SLMG Beverages currently has a gross turnover of around Rs 9,000 crore and expects to cross Rs 10,000 crore next year. It is targeting turnover of more than Rs 15,000 crore over the medium-term of three years, Ladhani said.

"We are currently growing at a double-digit rate and will continue the momentum. We grew about 25 per cent in FY26, while our compound annual growth rate (CAGR) has exceeded 20 per cent over the last four years,” Ladhani said, adding, "We are very bullish for growth."

On the investment front, SLMG has already invested around Rs 1,200 crore in its facility at Buxar in Bihar, while construction has begun at its proposed Gorakhpur plant in Uttar Pradesh, which will entail an investment of around Rs 1,000 crore.

"We have also acquired land for setting up bottling facilities in Central and Western UP. Construction will start in those plants very soon. Moreover, the second plant in Bihar will also come after 2027," he said.

SLMG Beverages, which had earlier announced investment of Rs 5,000 crore in UP and Bihar, "will be crossing that (committed amount ) in the next three years," Ladhani said.

The expansion is aimed at keeping pace with rising demand in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, where the company sees considerable headroom for growth, particularly in smaller towns and rural markets.

SLMG currently has bottling capacity of around 35,000 bottles per minute (BPM) and plans to add another 10,000 bottles per minute over the next five years.

"So, I think in the next five years, we will be adding another 10,000 BPM capacity… the way we are growing in the next 10 years, we should reach 1 lakh bottles per minute," said Ladhani.

Besides manufacturing, the company is investing in distribution and cooling infrastructure to improve product availability and expand consumption in underpenetrated markets.

It invested more than Rs 60-70 crore in chilling equipment last year and expects the overall investment in such equipment to exceed Rs 100 crore when its retailer financing initiative is included.

SLMG Beverages, which is among the top 15 Coca-Cola bottlers globally, holds bottling rights for Coca-Cola in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar along with Uttarakhand, and parts of Madhya Pradesh.

1.headline: EAAA India Alternatives to open Rs 1,200-crore IPO on October 26
1.heading: EAAA India Alternatives to open Rs 1,200-crore IPO on October 26
1.intro: EAAA India Alternatives IPO | The initial public offering comprises an offer-for-sale, closing on October 28, while the one-day anchor book for institutional investors will open on October 23.
1.body:
EAAA India Alternatives, erstwhile Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors, filed red herring prospectus with the Registrar of Companies intimating that its Rs 1,200-crore worth maiden public issue will hit Dalal Street on October 26.

The initial public offering (IPO) comprises an offer-for-sale (OFS), closing on October 28, while the one-day anchor book for institutional investors will open on October 23, as per the red herring prospectus filed on October 19.

Promoter entity Edelweiss Securities and Investments is a selling shareholder in the OFS. The issue proceeds, excluding offer expenses, will go to the said selling shareholder, and the company will not receive any funds from the IPO.

The issue size has been reduced from Rs 1,500 crore planned earlier as per the draft red herring prospectus filed in January 2026. Consequently, the draft document was cleared by capital markets regulator SEBI in April 2026.

The IPO share allotment is expected to be finalised by October 29, while the trading in its equity shares is likely to commence on the bourses on November 2.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

EAAA India Alternatives is an alternative asset manager focusing on two business verticals - real assets and private credit, with assets under management (AUM) of Rs 95,344.8 crore as of June 2026. Under the real assets segment, it invests in infrastructure and commercial real estate assets as well as energy assets through equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments, managing 10 active funds including two infrastructure investment trusts (InvITs), with a FPAUM (Fee-Paying Assets Under Management) of Rs 28.039.9 crore.

Further, private credit vertical primarily provides credit and flexible financing solutions, investing in debt or convertible debt instruments and secular instruments. The segment managed 16 active funds, with a FPAUM of Rs 19,272.4 crore.

The financial performance was healthy in the recent past periods, with profit growing 45 percent year-on-year to Rs 80.7 crore, and revenue increasing 44.4 percent to Rs 275.5 crore in the quarter ended June 2026. Profit soared 15.4 percent on-year to Rs 265.2 crore, and revenue surged 29.7 percent to Rs 869.5 crore in the year ended March 2026.

Axis Capital, Jefferies India, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, and Nuvama Wealth Management have been appointed as the merchant bankers for the EAAA India Alternatives IPO.

2.headline: Paras Healthcare mobilises Rs 652.5 crore via anchor book, Rs 1,450-crore IPO to open on October 21
2.heading: Paras Healthcare mobilises Rs 652.5 crore via anchor book, Rs 1,450-crore IPO to open on October 21
2.intro: Paras Healthcare IPO | The company allotted 94.15 lakh equity shares to 21 institutional investors through the anchor book on Monday.
2.body:
Paras Healthcare, the Gurugram-based hospital chain founded by Dr Dharminder Kumar Nagar, raised Rs 652.5 crore through its anchor book on October 19, ahead of the opening of its maiden public issue. Global investors participating in the anchor book included the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock Global Funds, Eastspring Investments, Government Pension Fund Global, Natixis International Funds, Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), and Citigroup Global.

The IPO will open for public subscription on October 21 and close on October 23. The price band has been fixed at Rs 660–693 per share.

The company plans to raise Rs 1,450 crore through the initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 950 crore. Promoter Dharminder Kumar Nagar and investor Commelina, an affiliate of private equity firm Creador, will sell shares worth Rs 300 crore and Rs 650 crore, respectively, through the OFS.

Paras Healthcare, which operates a network of eight hospitals under the Paras brand, allotted 94.15 lakh equity shares to 21 institutional investors through the anchor book on Monday.

"Of these, 55.55 lakh shares worth Rs 385 crore were allocated to nine domestic mutual funds, which participated through a total of 24 schemes," the company said in its filing.

The domestic mutual funds that participated in the anchor book included SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC AMC, ICICI Prudential AMC, Kotak Mahindra AMC, WhiteOak Capital, Motilal Oswal AMC, Edelweiss, Baroda BNP Paribas Mutual Fund, and ITI Mutual Fund.

Insurance companies, including ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Edelweiss Life Insurance, and Canara HSBC Life Insurance, also participated in the anchor book, acquiring 6.49 lakh shares worth Rs 45 crore.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Paras Healthcare provides tertiary and quaternary healthcare services through a network of eight hospitals with a total capacity of 2,211 beds across North India, Bihar, and Jharkhand.

As part of its expansion plans, the company intends to add a 300-bed hospital in Gurugram and a 500-bed hospital in Ludhiana. The two facilities are expected to become operational in the current and next financial years, respectively.

According to the company's red herring prospectus (RHP), Paras Healthcare expects to increase its total bed capacity to 3,011 by March 2028.

The company plans to utilise Rs 375 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue to repay a portion of its debt, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

JM Financial, BofA Securities India, and Nuvama Wealth Management are acting as the merchant bankers to the Paras Healthcare IPO.
